beats: Inspecting the western folded nets before agreeing to help only reveals the smooth-handled shuttle; the player does not take it unasked.

beats.description: Sella asks the child to find the shuttle before the tide does.

options.description: Agree and work it free from the folded nets without cutting them. If it cannot fit in the bag, return after making room.
Decline or leave. Sella can be asked again; the tide wording does not start a timer or destroy the tool.

beats: Return the shuttle. Sella turns it over, notices the three cuts and tells how her brother relearned his work after losing two fingers to a winch.
Accept the Silk Scarf reward when there is room. Later conversation explains how often her brother repaired it.
data.consequences: Returning the shuttle completes its recovery even when the scarf cannot fit. Sella keeps that unpaid reward available; neither the net search nor the handover must be repeated. The tool and scarf cannot be collected repeatedly. The errand survives leaving and saving and is not a gate to the ring, museum or crossing.

dialogue.context: Existing dialogue. When the shuttle is returned.
dialogue.text:
Sella: My brother's. He lost two fingers to a winch, then taught himself all over again.
Sella: People at the ring call that sort of thing a good story. He mostly called it inconvenient.

description: An optional search for a working tool lets Sella speak about her brother through marks, repairs and use. The quest keeps his injury separate from the ring crowd’s appetite for a good story; returning what she needs produces a particular gift rather than a confession about the world’s mythology.
